Mostly law professors | Sometimes contrarian | Often libertarian | Always independent

New news! This month, IJ client Libby Souder asked the South Carolina Supreme Court to let her resume teaching private swim lessons in her backyard pool, which she'd done for years with city approval and without incident. The city still can't show the ban serves a legitimate purpose, and one day they're going to have to. (Or they could, you know, repeal the thing.) Click here to learn more.

#7715. The Election Integrity Scorecard: Progress and the Path Forward

Election integrity remains essential to ensuring that Americans have confidence in the electoral process. This program will review the 2026 Election Integrity Scorecard, highlighting key results, notable progress, and areas where further work is needed. Experts and state leaders will discuss election reforms, lessons learned across the country, and the challenges and opportunities ahead. The conversation will explore how states can continue strengthening election laws, improving election administration, and promoting transparency and accountability in the democratic process.

A distinguished lineup of speakers will also preview the upcoming Supreme Court oral argument in Mi Familia Vota v. RNC, addressing whether documentary proof-of-citizenship requirements are preempted by the National Voter Registration Act and whether noncitizens may be removed from voter rolls during the 90-day quiet period under federal law. Panelists will discuss opportunities for continued reform of citizenship-verification requirements in voter registration and voting.

Join us for a discussion of the current election integrity landscape, the significance of the latest Scorecard results, and how policymakers and election officials can build on recent progress to help ensure elections are secure, fair, and worthy of public confidence.

#7714. The 2026 Russell Kirk Lecture Featuring Dr. Bradley Birzer

From Heraclitus forward, Western civilization has understood the imagination as one of our highest faculties of knowing. We know through our mind (rationality) and through our stomach (passions), but it’s the chest (the heart or the soul) that bridges both. In his lecture, Tolkien, "Lewis, Kirk, Mythos, and Logos," Dr. Bradley Birzer will examine the ways in which imagination has shaped conservatism and tradition, especially through the key figures of Russell Kirk, C.S. Lewis, and J.R.R. Tolkien.

The namesake of the lecture, famed scholar Russell Kirk (1918–1994), established the philosophical foundations of the modern conservative movement with his landmark books, The Conservative Mind (1953) and The Roots of American Order (1974). He was instrumental in the founding of National Review and Modern Age and was a distinguished fellow of The Heritage Foundation.

Kirk’s political philosophy, summarized in his “six cannons of conservatism,” emphasized tradition and convention, transcendence and piety, political prudence, and ordered liberty. His application of those canons to contemporary issues, through essays, lectures, and newspaper columns, was often provocative and controversial, but always noteworthy. Today, his works and legacy are being preserved and advanced by The Russell Kirk Center for Cultural Renewal. The Russell Kirk Lecture Series recognizes eminent thinkers in the tradition of “the father of American conservatism.”
